architecture_summary.operational_context: cloud-hosted multi-tenant LLM agent fleet with third-party model APIs and self-hosted model option

threat_actors.name: External Opportunistic Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Credential harvesting, service abuse, data exfiltration for resale
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Phishing tenant credentials or exploiting public API vulnerabilities
non_capabilities: No physical access to cloud infrastructure
No zero-day exploits for cloud provider services
No insider knowledge of tenant data schemas

threat_actors.name: Targeted Adversary (APT-style)
threat_actors.motivation: Intellectual property theft, persistent access to tenant conversations and vector embeddings
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Supply chain compromise of third-party model API or malicious prompt injection via tenant input
non_capabilities: No direct access to self-hosted LLM infrastructure
No ability to modify AuditLog integrity controls
No nation-state level zero-day budget for custom model backdoors

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider (Tenant Admin)
threat_actors.motivation: Exfiltrate other tenants' data, escalate privileges across tenant boundary
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate tenant admin credentials with elevated API access
non_capabilities: No access to underlying cloud control plane
No ability to bypass PromptGuard or ResponseFilter logic
No direct database admin access to TenantDB

threat_actors.name: Adversarial Agent (Prompt Injection)
threat_actors.motivation: Goal hijacking, tool misuse, data exfiltration via agent autonomy
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Malicious user input crafted to override LLMOrchestrator system prompt
non_capabilities: Cannot directly invoke ModelRouter without PromptGuard evaluation
Cannot write to AuditLog or modify TenantDB schema
Cannot access other tenants' VectorDB namespaces without TenantRouter authorization

attack_paths.impact: Unauthenticated access to tenant routing logic, potential bypass of RateLimiter
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: API Gateway is internet-exposed; known CVEs in gateway software provide exploitable surface

attack_paths.impact: Access to tenant-scoped LLMOrchestrator, ConversationStore, VectorDB
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Credential theft via phishing is prevalent; tenant keys often stored insecurely in client apps

attack_paths.impact: Goal hijacking: agent ignores PromptGuard, invokes ModelRouter with malicious instructions, exfiltrates VectorDB data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Prompt injection is a proven class of attacks against LLM agents; PromptGuard may not catch novel obfuscation

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised model server via supply chain or RCE in inference framework
attack_paths.impact: Persistent foothold in internal model backend, bypass third-party API controls
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Self-hosted model runs in isolated VPC; requires supply chain compromise or unpatched inference server vulnerability

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised LLMOrchestrator with excessive DB permissions
attack_paths.impact: Cross-tenant data access, modification of tenant configurations
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: If LLMOrchestrator uses shared DB credentials with broad grants, lateral movement to TenantDB is feasible

attack_paths.entry_point: LLMOrchestrator tool call to VectorDB query
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of tenant embeddings containing proprietary data, PII, trade secrets
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: VectorDB stores semantic representations of confidential data; agent has legitimate query access

attack_paths.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Command and Control Channel
attack_paths.entry_point: ModelRouter forwarding crafted prompts to OpenAI API
attack_paths.impact: Data exfiltration via model responses; attacker encodes stolen data in model output
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Third-party model APIs are egress channels; ResponseFilter may not detect steganographic encoding

attack_paths.entry_point: Poisoned fine-tuning data or malicious model artifact
attack_paths.impact: Persistent malicious behavior triggered by specific prompts; bypasses PromptGuard
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires compromise of model training pipeline or artifact supply chain; self-hosted model reduces exposure

attack_paths.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_paths.entry_point: Adversarial prompt causing LLMOrchestrator to skip PromptGuard call
attack_paths.impact: Bypass of input sanitization; subsequent prompts reach ModelRouter unfiltered
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Agent tool-calling logic may be subverted if PromptGuard invocation is not enforced architecturally

attack_paths.entry_point: LLMOrchestrator tool call with malicious delete instruction
attack_paths.impact: Destruction of tenant conversation history, audit trail gaps
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires agent to have delete permissions and be tricked into invoking them; ResponseFilter may block

mitigations.control_name: Identities and credentials are managed for authorized devices and users
Users, devices, and other assets are authenticated commensurate with risk
Maintain an inventory of authentication systems
A baseline configuration of information technology/industrial control systems is created and maintained
The network is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
Model provenance verification and integrity checking
Access permissions are managed, incorporating the principle of least privilege
Response filtering for sensitive data detection
Response plans and recovery plans are in place and managed

findings.severity_rationale: Prompt injection against LLMOrchestrator can bypass PromptGuard and lead to unauthorized tool use and data exfiltration; PromptGuard is only partially implemented
VectorDB contains confidential tenant embeddings; LLMOrchestrator has broad query access with insufficient tenant isolation at the data layer
Third-party model APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic) serve as uncontrolled egress channels; ResponseFilter only partially detects steganographic exfiltration
Self-hosted LLM model artifact integrity not verified; supply chain compromise could implant persistent backdoor
Tenant API keys are high-value targets; credential theft enables full tenant-scoped access to LLM agent and data stores
API Gateway vulnerability exploitation requires specific CVE; mitigated by patch management and WAF
ConversationStore destruction requires agent to have delete permissions and be tricked; least privilege and ResponseFilter reduce likelihood
AuditLog integrity is critical for forensics; LLMOrchestrator and PromptGuard write to it but no tamper-evidence controls declared

agentic.blast_radius: Single tenant's conversation history, vector embeddings, and configuration; potential cross-tenant data access if TenantRouter authorization bypassed; third-party model API egress
human_oversight_points: Tenant admin approval for agent configuration changes
AuditLog review for anomalous tool call patterns
No real-time human-in-the-loop for individual prompt processing
